Article Title: How Bangladesh beat lure of white-ball riches to save its Tests
Article Text:
The Test win in Darwin is the realisation of the talent and the immaculate process focusing on Test cricket put in place by the BCB.

Changing pitches in domestic cricket

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Hiring legends as fast bowling coaches

Days before the Darwin Test against Bangladesh, Australia captain Pat Cummins had said in a podcast: “Some of our guys are saying no to half-a-million pounds for 20 days’ work to go and play those two Test matches against Bangladesh. I think it is a tension point. At the moment our guys are so keen to play for Australia that they’re happy to forgo that, but I don’t think we can accept that that is going to be the case forever.’”Cummins, the proud face of arguably the best fast-bowling attack in Tests today, was only reminding us aloud how the dynamics of world cricket have drastically changed over the last decade. But, it was Bangladesh cricket that quietly chose to go the other way during that period, a move that ironically culminated in mowing down Cummins’ powerhouse Test team on their own soil on Sunday.In doing so, six months after forfeiting their T20 World Cup place due to diplomatic reasons, they have made this World Test Championship cycle the most exciting one since its inception in 2019.Bangladesh’s pace resources have now become the talk of the cricket town. They had shown their potential in demolishing Pakistan — both at home and away in last two years.The Test win in Darwin is the realisation of the talent and the immaculate process focusing on Test cricket put in place by the Bangladesh Cricket Board (BCB).“Even (as recently as) fivesix years ago, pacers didn’t want to play Test cricket. They were happy playing just whiteball cricket. The BCB decided to incentivise Test cricket. Special contracts were drawn where the pacers could make a fancy living by playing Tests,” former Bangladesh captain and current chief selector Habibul Bashar, who led the team when Bangladesh beat Australia in an ODI for the first time in 2005, told TOI from Darwin.BCB changed the match fee and contract structure in 2019. Till then, ODI players were the best paid which resulted in fast bowlers backing out of Test cricket.The board decided to rework the contracts in a way that saw Test players become the highest paid cricketers in the country. The fee for a Test match has been doubled from 4 lakh Bangladeshi Taka to 8 lakh Bangladeshi Taka.“Now, our fast bowlers preserve themselves for Test cricket. They don’t run after contracts in T20 leagues. If a T20 league contract comes, the BCB assesses if the player can be released,” said Bashar.Now, Bangladesh have a battery of pacers who come from humble backgrounds. Tearaway quick Nahid Rana comes from a remote village in Rajshahi close to the India border and Hasan Mahmud is from Lakshmipur in Chittagong while Ebadot Hossain and Tanzim Shakib are from Sylhet.The word in Bangladesh cricket is that they don’t want bowlers going the Mustafizur Rahman way who didn’t prioritise Test cricket for playing in T20 leagues.The trigger point in the pace revolution came in 2014-15.Over the last decade, former Bangladesh captain Akram Khan, Bashar and Minhajul Abedin got working on domestic cricket in various capacities like chief selector, head of cricket operations and BCB director.“The domestic pitches used to be bare and spinner-friendly. The teams would play three spinners and one pacer. We worked on the grounds and decided to make it a rule of having at least 6-mm grass on the pitches.“We also made it compulsory for teams to play three pacers in first-class matches. It encouraged these bowlers from the outskirts to bowl fast. When the pitches became pacer-friendly, teams organically started picking more pacers,” Bashar said.Bangladesh cricket’s primary pipeline is U-19 cricket. When fast bowlers are spotted at that level, the board takes over their journey.However, a big point in Bangladesh’s pace-bowling revolution has been hiring big international bowlers as fast bowling coaches.“We brought in Courtney Walsh, Heath Streak and Allan Donald as fast bowling coaches. Their presence with the national team made a huge difference.“At the same time, we encouraged domestic coaches to spend time with them too. That knowledge passed on and helped in shaping raw fast bowlers,” Bashar claimed, subtly highlighting their ecosystem’s unique thinking that is creating a reverse revolution in cricket.
Article Summary: Bangladesh's pace resources have now become the talk of the cricket town. The Test win in Darwin is the realisation of the talent and the immaculate process focusing on Test cricket put in place by the Bangladesh Cricket Board. The trigger point in the pace revolution came in 2014-15.

Article Title: AUS vs BAN 2nd Test: Australia make major change to squad after shock Bangladesh defeat
Article Text:
AFP Photo

Renshaw gets Test recall

Labuschagne under pressure

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Inglis, Boland retain places

Australia squad vs Bangladesh

Australia have made one change to their squad for the second and final ICC World Test Championship match against Bangladesh in Mackay.Opener Jake Weatherald has been left out of the 13-player squad, with left-hander Matthew Renshaw coming in as his replacement.If selected, Renshaw will make his first Test appearance for Australia in more than three years.The 30-year-old last played a Test in Delhi against India in 2023, when he came in as a concussion substitute for regular opener David Warner.Renshaw has since represented Australia in both ODI and T20I cricket. He now returns to the Test squad after Australia's top order struggled in the first Test against Bangladesh.Australia were bowled out for just 198 in their first innings, while Weatherald managed scores of only 23 and zero in the match.Regular No.3 Marnus Labuschagne has retained his place in the squad. However, Australia coach Andrew McDonald admitted that the batter needs to score more runs to secure his place in the team."I think it was 31 he got in the second innings, and up until the point he got out, you'd sit there and say he was looking good," McDonald said of Labuschagne."He was moving well, he's clipping off his pads, he was getting back through the ball down the ground.So it's easy for me to sit here and try to defend that, but ultimately it's 31. It's not a big score. He's lacked runs. He feels that. We feel that. We're working incredibly hard as a coaching group."Back-up wicketkeeper-batter Josh Inglis and reserve bowler Scott Boland have also retained their places in the squad.Both players could come into contention for the second Test, which begins on Saturday.Pat Cummins (c), Scott Boland, Alex Carey, Cameron Green, Josh Hazlewood, Travis Head, Josh Inglis, Marnus Labuschagne, Nathan Lyon, Matthew Renshaw, Steve Smith, Mitchell Starc, Beau Webster.
Article Summary: Australia have made one change to their squad for the second and final ICC World Test Championship match against Bangladesh. Opener Jake Weatherald has been left out of the 13-player squad. Matthew Renshaw will make his first Test appearance for Australia in more than three years. Regular No.3 Marnus Labuschagne has retained his place in the squad.

Article Title: BWF World Championships: Ayush Shetty stuns World No. 1 Shi Yu Qi; India 5-0 on Day 1
Article Text:
Ayush Shetty with fans (PTI Photo)

Ayush Shetty (ANI Photo)

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

New Delhi: The last time Ayush Shetty was up against Shi Yu Qi, he was rendered clueless. In a contest that lasted only 42 minutes at the Asia Championships in April, Shetty could only win 18 points, extending the head-to-head in favour of the Chinese to 3-0. The overwhelming feeling was that the World No. 22 wasn't allowed to play his usual powerful, smash-laden game."Shi Yu Qi in the first round is better than him in the later round," said legendary Pullela Gopichand when the draw was made. "With his big smash, I think Ayush is definitely going to be quite a threat. I do believe he has a very good chance," he continued.On Monday, in front of a partisan crowd, Shetty proved him right in sensational fashion. The Indian produced stuff of dreams to beat the top seed and defending BWF World Championships winner 21-14, 13-21, 21-19 in an edge-of-the-seat thriller.In what was billed as the biggest match of the day and the first round, playing in his maiden World Championships, Shetty timed his smashes to perfection and his lifts with absolute precision. In tricky conditions, with both sides of the court behaving differently, the two-time Worlds medallist had his smashes blocked dutifully and struggled against the Karnataka native's aggressive display.With the duo splitting games, the physical aspect of Shetty's game was tested in the 73-minute match.But perhaps more than that, it was his mental fortitude that came to the fore. Having built an 11-5 lead in the decider, which was then extended to 16-5, Shetty rode a comeback wave from the Chinese shuttler. Shi Yu Qi won 10 of the next 12 points to bring the deficit down to just three points."I was telling myself to calm down. I was getting a bit nervous because he was really catching up and the momentum was with him. And everything I did, he somehow managed to retrieve it. So I was just telling myself to calm down and be aggressive," explained Shetty later.The feeling on the other end was one of confidence, with the drift coming to the rescue as well. The nerves from the Indian also played into Yu Qi's hands. A simple put-away was thrown into the net. A deep return was left alone, which ended up landing in.Little by little, the five match points at 20-15 became just one. On his fifth match point, Shetty cleverly used his wrist to leave Yu Qi stranded, sending the shuttle away from his reach and the crowd into absolute delirium.Easy win for PV Sindhu , India go 5-0 on Day 1While Ayush Shetty was the star attraction of the day, the rest of the Indian contingent, too, made a flawless start at the prestigious competition. PV Sindhu romped past Sophia Noble 21-7, 21-11 in 29 minutes, while the doubles pairings of Hariharan Amsakarunan-MR Arjun, Treesa Jolly-Gayatri Pullela Gopichand and Kavipriya Selvam-Simran Singhi made it into their respective next rounds.ALSO READ: 'It's a lady's sport': The challenge of badminton in Uganda, Canada, Bulgaria "I think overall, playing for the first time, it was important for me to get used to the court conditions and see how it is. Today, I think that was the first thing for me that came into my mind. But I think I managed it well and the court conditions are pretty good," said Sindhu, who will play Canada's Wen Yu Zhang next.
Article Summary: Ayush Shetty beats Shi Yu Qi 21-14, 13-21, 21-19 in an edge-of-the-seat thriller. Shetty timed his smashes to perfection and his lifts with absolute precision. PV Sindhu and Hariharan Amsakarunan also made a flawless start.

Article Title: Hockey World Cup: ‘Show a bit of composure’ — Fulton’s message to India ahead of must-not-lose Pakistan clash
Article Text:
Team India (Pic credit: Hockey India)

Fulton calls for composure against Pakistan

Manpreet stresses defensive discipline

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: India head coach Craig Fulton has urged his side to show greater composure and sharpen their defensive discipline against Pakistan after England exposed their weaknesses in a 2-4 defeat in their second Pool D match of the Hockey World Cup on Monday.India produced a strong first half and led 2-1 at the break after goals from Harmanpreet Singh and Dilpreet Singh. But England turned the contest around after half-time, scoring three times to leave India needing at least a point against Pakistan in their final pool match on Wednesday to progress to the second round.Fulton admitted India’s defensive intensity dropped after the interval.“The first half was good. We got PCs on the counter-attack and came back nicely with a bit more control. In the third quarter our defence was not as good as it was supposed to be,” Fulton said after the match.“England played like a world number three team. We created a few chances but couldn't convert those.”The India coach was quick to shift focus to the Pakistan game, recognising the importance of Wednesday’s clash. India have three points from two matches after beating Wales in their opener, while Pakistan have one point.“If we had won today, we still have to do the business in the next game. We just have to be better on the ball in the final match and show a bit of composure. We needed to press out and put some pressure on them,” he said.“The forward line played well but we needed to score three-plus goals and we could only score two. It's just the second match and we will learn from this loss. We have another big opportunity against Pakistan and the boys are motivated for that.”India had taken control of the contest after falling behind in the first quarter. Nicholas Bandurak put England ahead in the 14th minute before Harmanpreet equalised from a penalty corner. Dilpreet then completed the turnaround in the second quarter.England, however, dominated the third quarter. Stuart Rushmere levelled in the 39th minute before Henry Croft put England ahead four minutes later. Bandurak added his second from a penalty corner in the 55th minute to seal the victory.Experienced midfielder Manpreet Singh also pointed to defensive lapses as a key reason for the defeat and warned India cannot afford similar mistakes against Pakistan.“We were playing so well till the third quarter but there were a few defensive lapses in the last quarter which cost us. Overall, the performance was good but the defence has to be very strong against the top teams and we need to convert our chances also,” Manpreet said.India tried several variations from penalty corners, but England’s defence stood firm.“We were trying variations on PCs but they defended well. We cannot underestimate any team. Pakistan also have good penalty corner specialists, so we must not concede PCs against them. We have to earn more PCs in the upcoming matches,” he said.Manpreet also stressed that India continued to create opportunities despite England’s pressure.“Our defenders broke their full press many times. It's a long tournament and we will learn from the mistakes. You cannot play with the same momentum for the whole 60 minutes, but we are creating opportunities till the last minute. There is a structure of playing and we follow that,” he said.With England now sitting at the top of Pool D with two wins, India’s attention turns firmly to Pakistan. A draw would be enough to take India through, while defeat would end their campaign.
Article Summary: India lost 2-4 to England in their second Pool D match of the Hockey World Cup on Monday. India coach Craig Fulton has urged his side to show greater composure and sharpen their defensive discipline against Pakistan. India need at least a point against Pakistan in their final pool match on Wednesday to progress to the second round.

Article Title: 23 state equestrian bodies seek time-bound EFI elections, flag governance concerns
Article Text:
Equestrian Federation of India (EFI)

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: As many as 23 state and union territory equestrian associations have called for a time-bound election process to restore an elected and representative administration at the Equestrian Federation of India (EFI), amid growing concerns over the prolonged governance uncertainty in the sport.The associations met at a New Delhi hotel on Aug 15 and unanimously adopted four resolutions, covering EFI elections, the functioning of the Ad Hoc Committee, transparency in decision-making and the inclusion of equestrian sport in the National Games and Khelo India Youth Games.The meeting came against the backdrop of the National Sports Governance Act, 2025, and the National Sports Governance (National Sports Bodies) Rules, 2026. The participating associations said the continuing uncertainty was neither in the interests of Indian equestrian sport nor its athletes and urged the Indian Olympic Association (IOA), Ministry of Youth Affairs and Sports (MYAS) and the International Equestrian Federation (FEI) to intervene.The most significant demand was for the Ad Hoc Committee overseeing the EFI to announce a definite election schedule and complete the electoral process at the earliest.The associations pointed to a three-month timeline for elections after the committee's constitution, claiming that the deadline had lapsed on June 26 without a formal extension from either the Delhi High Court or the IOA.They also raised concerns over changes in the composition of the four-member Ad Hoc Committee, stating that at least two members had exited and replacements had not been named. The associations urged the sports ministry to direct the IOA to take responsibility for conducting the EFI elections in line with the applicable legal framework and recent court directions.Another resolution questioned the Ad Hoc Committee's authority to take policy decisions in areas such as selection criteria, allocation of events in the annual calendar and tournament or entry fees. The state bodies maintained that such policy matters fall within the domain of the EFI General Body and pointed out that no General Body meeting had been held since August 2024.The associations further demanded greater transparency, calling for the publication of minutes of meetings of the Ad Hoc Committee and any sub-committees constituted by it.The meeting also highlighted the sport's achievements and its struggle for greater recognition at the domestic level. Indian equestrian athletes have won 14 Asian Games medals — four gold, three silver and seven bronze — while the country secured five medals at the 2025 Asian Equestrian Championships, including one gold and four silver.Despite that record, the associations noted that equestrian sport has not been included in the National Games or Khelo India Youth Games. They urged the IOA to include the discipline in every edition of the National Games and the MYAS and Sports Authority of India to ensure its inclusion in every Khelo India Youth Games.The associations also proposed a seven-member sub-committee to represent state bodies before the MYAS, IOA and FEI. Representatives from Gujarat, Karnataka, Assam, Madhya Pradesh, Maharashtra, Uttarakhand and Delhi were proposed for the panel.
Article Summary: As many as 23 state and union territory equestrian associations have called for a time-bound election process to restore an elected and representative administration at the Equestrian Federation of India. The associations met at a New Delhi hotel on Aug 15 and unanimously adopted four resolutions, covering EFI elections, the functioning of the Ad Hoc Committee, transparency in decision- making and the inclusion of equestrians in the National Games and Khelo India Youth Games.

Article Title: Maharashtra gymnastics body seeks financial clarity from GFI, cites licence fees, grants
Article Text:
Gymnastics Federation of India (GFI)

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: The Maharashtra Amateur Gymnastics Association (MAGA), an affiliated member of the Gymnastics Federation of India (GFI), has sought detailed financial and accounting clarifications from the national federation, raising questions over the accounting of licence fees, govt grants and affiliation income for the financial year 2024-25.In a communication to GFI president Sudhir Mittal, the Maharashtra body has sought documentary records and reconciled financial figures, stressing that transparency is essential for a national sports federation handling membership and competition-related fees as well as government funds.Among the key issues flagged is the GFI's audited financial statement for the year ended March 31, 2025. MAGA has asked the federation to disclose which competent authority reviewed and approved the accounts and whether the audited financials were placed before and approved by the GFI General Body. It has also sought the minutes of any such meeting.Questions have also allegedly been raised over the appointment of Narender Singh & Co, chartered accountants, as statutory auditors for 2024-25, including the authority that made the appointment, the audit fee fixed and whether the appointment was approved by the General Body.A major point of contention is the absence of licence-fee income in the financial statement.MAGA alleged that GFI collected Rs 1,000 per gymnast as a licence fee for participation in national championships and says the Maharashtra association facilitated payments for more than 220 gymnasts across disciplines and age groups. It has sought details of the total licence fees collected during 2024-25 and their utilisation.The association has similarly sought clarification over the apparent absence of affiliation-fee income and govt assistance from the income-and-expenditure account. It has asked for details of grants and financial assistance received from the Sports Authority of India and the union sports ministry, along with their accounting and utilisation.MAGA has also sought details of the GFI Finance Committee, including its present composition and the authority under which it was constituted, besides information on mechanisms to disclose conflicts of interest and related-party transactions involving office-bearers, executive committee members or their relatives.The development comes against the backdrop of a Feb 2026 show-cause notice issued to GFI by the ministry. The ministry had cited repeated delays in submission of proposals and utilisation certificates relating to govt grants, failure to empanel qualified coaches and support staff, inadequate planning for foreign exposure and national coaching camps, and complaints alleging non-transparent and unfair athlete-selection processes.GFI was asked to explain within 15 days why action under the Sports Code should not be taken.MAGA, while saying its latest communication is not intended to prejudge any office-bearer, has asked GFI to acknowledge the request and provide a timeline for furnishing the information. It warned that failure to respond could prompt escalation of the matter to the appropriate authorities.The association has maintained that its demand is aimed at financial accountability and transparency, particularly in view of the interests of athletes, coaches, state associations and other stakeholders in Indian gymnastics.
Article Summary: The Maharashtra Amateur Gymnastics Association (MAGA) has sought detailed financial and accounting clarifications from the national federation. It has raised questions over the accounting of licence fees, govt grants and affiliation income for the financial year 2024-25. The development comes against the backdrop of a Feb 2026 show-cause notice issued to GFI.

Article Title: Air of discontent: Anders Antonsen wants India Open moved out of Delhi winter
Article Text:
New Delhi: Denmark's Anders Antonsen (PTI)

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: Anders Antonsen has returned to Delhi with a victory — and a familiar warning for the Badminton World Federation (BWF): if the India Open remains in the capital’s winter months, he would rather pay the fine than breathe through another tournament.The Danish world No. 4, a four-time World Championships medallist, has skipped the India Open for the last three editions, including this year, and was fined $5,000 for his latest withdrawal. His objection, he stressed after beating Azerbaijan’s Dicky Dwi Pangestu 21-19, 21-17 at the ongoing Worlds on Monday, is not to Delhi but to its Jan-Feb air.“In Jan and Feb, the pollution here is quite insane. It’s not pleasant to play in. You kind of get this burning feeling in your throat,” Antonsen said. “Imagine having your pulse high and trying to fight for air. It’s not a pleasant feeling.”The contrast with Aug has only strengthened his argument. “If I was the BWF, I would host the India Open at another time of the year,” he said, adding that the conditions now are “way better”. "When I open the blinds in the morning, I can see stuff," he added.Antonsen has accepted that his stance could again cost him.“When I see the calendar, I’m like, okay, they’re all instantly giving me a $5,000 fine.”Mia Blichfeldt, meanwhile, finds herself in a different bind despite sharing concerns about Delhi’s conditions. The Dane, returning after knee problems, advanced with a 21-18, 21-4 win over Azerbaijan’s Keisha Fatimah Azzahra but cannot simply walk away from a Super 750.“No, I will not do that because I am not in the same position like him. It's the rankings...I can’t miss out playing a 750 tournament,” she said.Mia believes conditions are “better” now, allowing her to focus on performance. Antonsen can opt out; Mia cannot. Their message, however, is similar: Delhi may be manageable in summer, but winter pollution should not be part of the BWF season.
Article Summary: Anders Antonsen says he would rather pay a $5,000 fine than play another tournament in Delhi. The Danish world No. 4 has skipped the India Open for the last three editions. He beat Azerbaijan’s Dicky Dwi Pangestu 21-19, 21-17 at the ongoing Worlds on Monday.

Article Title: Parents back in the stands after 13 years, M R Arjun eyes medal at home BWF Championships
Article Text:
India's Hariharan Amsakarunan and M R Arjun (ANI Photo)

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: For M R Arjun, advancing to the second round of the BWF World Championships was satisfying. But the sight that awaited him in the stands of the Indira Gandhi (IG) indoor stadium here made Monday’s victory feel rather more personal.For the first time in nearly 13 years, Arjun’s parents watched him play live at a major tournament. Both retired only a few months ago from their govt and teaching jobs. They are now in the stands, alongside Arjun's wife, as their son embarks on a Worlds campaign on home soil.“It would probably be 13 years later that both would be coming in,” Arjun told TOI. “Both my mom and dad retired 2-3 months back and then I told them, what is your plan if all you guys are free? This big event is happening on our home soil. So both of them are very much excited.”His father was once a familiar figure at Arjun’s junior tournaments, travelling with him from around the age of eight. But as Arjun grew older, he chose to travel with coaches and fellow players, believing it was better for his development. "My dad used to take me around for all my junior matches...but after that, I had the opinion that I would love playing alone or travelling alone,” he recalled.Work commitments then kept his parents away. His mother, a teacher, found it difficult to take leave, while Arjun’s father remained occupied with his govt job. “My mom takes so much pressure watching,” Arjun said with a smile. “She used to get tense and all of that.”Now, with both parents retired, their presence has given this championship an added emotional resonance. “Definitely,” Arjun said when asked if seeing them in the stadium was an added motivation. "I would love to medal for them."His wife, whom he married in Feb, has also become a constant pillar of support, travelling with him to tournaments since their wedding. “She has come for a few tournaments, Malaysia, Indonesia,” he said.On court, Arjun and Hariharan Amsakarunan began their campaign on a winning note. The duo was leading 6-4 in the second game, when their opponents Scott Guildea and Paul Reynolds of Ireland retired hurt.Earlier, Arjun and Amsakarunan won the first game 21-16."As soon as we entered, we started hearing the cheer,” Arjun said. “This is going to be extra energy for us.” For Arjun, however, the most cherished cheer may come from the stands where, after all these years, his parents are finally watching him live again.
Article Summary: M R Arjun and Hariharan Amsakarunan advanced to the second round of the BWF World Championships. For the first time in nearly 13 years, Arjun’s parents watched him play live at a major tournament. Both retired only a few months ago from their govt and teaching jobs.

Article Title: 4-2 defeat to England leaves India with no room for error against Pakistan
Article Text:
India lose 2-4 to England. (Pic credit: Hockey India)

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Result: England: 4 (Nicolas Bandurak 14, 55; Stuart Rushmere 39; Henry Croft 43) bt India 2 (Harmanpreet Singh 17, Dilpreet Singh 25).

It took England striker Nicholas Bandurak nine years to graduate from the junior to the senior national team. In the intervening years, he spent plenty of time watching and learning from some of the best in the business. One player he followed keenly was Indian skipper Harmanpreet Singh On Monday at the Wagener Hockey Stadium in Amstelveen, Netherlands, the Englishman of Ukrainian roots turned tutor as India went from impressive to disastrous. The 33-year-old scored a field goal, converted a penalty corner and provided crucial assists, each a key lesson for the Indians.In their second Pool outing at the FIH World Cup, the men in saffron paid a heavy price for elementary mistakes, surrendering a 2-1 lead to lose 2-4. The loss left Craig Fulton’s men in a must-win situation in their final league fixture against Pakistan on Wednesday.As expected, the contest began as a tug-of-war, with the anchors and pullers on either side throwing everything into the battle. Abhishek and Jarmanpreet Singh made a couple of impressive early inroads, but failed to turn them into goals.Bandurak, who made his World Cup debut in India in 2023, broke the deadlock in the 14th minute.Stuart Rushmere, another of England’s standout performers, brought down a long pass from deep and fed Bandurak, who had already outfoxed the Indian defenders and positioned himself perfectly to finish.India pressed hard, but England’s midfielders made it difficult for them to find a way through. Two minutes into the second quarter, however, Harmanpreet restored parity, finding the top-left corner with surgical precision.The repeated attacks down the flanks finally paid off when Abhishek took Hardik Singh’s free hit in the striking circle. Dilpreet Singh applied a deft touch to put India ahead.India went into the half-time break with a 2-1 advantage.But the warning signs were already there. England quickly worked out India’s defensive ploy as the latter tried to protect their lead.With India rotating goalkeepers every quarter, HS Mohith returned after the break. England immediately put him under pressure, and the youngster left angles exposed. Amit Rohidas and Jugraj Singh also struggled in the backline, conceding penalty corners that allowed England to build momentum.Rushmere made India pay, equalising with an artistic reverse flick after a sweeping pass exposed a chink in the Indian defence.England thrived on aerial balls and Rushmere brought one of them down with precision before finding Henry Croft in front of Mohith. The ball was slotted home with little fuss to put England ahead in the 43rd minute.Five minutes before the final hoot, Bandurak put the result beyond doubt, converting a set piece with a low flick that went beyond the reach of last-quarter goalkeeper Suraj Karkera.
Article Summary: Nicolas Bandurak scored a field goal, converted a penalty corner and provided crucial assists. Stuart Rushmere made India pay, equalising with an artistic reverse flick after a sweeping pass exposed a chink in the Indian defence. Henry Croft slotted home with little fuss to put England ahead.

Article Title: Dilip Tirkey breaks silence on World Cup absence amid Hockey India controversy
Article Text:
New Delhi, July 31 (IANS) Hockey India president Dilip Tirkey

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

With Hockey India secretary general Bhola Nath Singh and embattled director general RK Srivastava currently in the Netherlands for the FIH World Cup, questions have been raised about HI president Dilip Tirkey's absence from the tournament.Ongoing controversies within the federation and his face-off with Srivastava over the jersey colour-change row have brought the former Indian skipper’s absence into focus. Putting the speculation to rest, Tirkey told TOI: “I had informed the Executive Board well in advance that I would not travel for the World Cup because of the next edition of the Hockey India League (HIL). The league is crucial for exposure and the growth of both men’s and women’s hockey in the country.“I could not have stayed away from the country for a long period,” he added.“In fact, on Monday, treasurer Sekar Manoharan and I met potential stakeholders in Mumbai. I would have loved to be in the Netherlands, but my presence here was more essential,” Tirkey said.The HIL, a franchise-based league, was revived in 2024 under Tirkey’s leadership after a seven-year hiatus. While the league has attracted some of the top stars from around the world, it has also faced a host of challenges, including issues related to ownership, sponsorship and logistics.The upcoming edition could face further uncertainty as there are talks about a couple of franchises opting out.
Article Summary: Dilip Tirkey is currently in the Netherlands for the FIH World Cup. Questions have been raised about the HI president's absence from the tournament. Tirkey told TOI that he would not travel for the World Cup because of the next edition of the Hockey India League (HIL)

Article Title: World Cup victory fuels India's hunger, Jemimah Rodrigues sets sights on Champions Trophy 2027
Article Text:
Jemimah eyes Champions Trophy glory (Agency Image)

'Champions Trophy is going to be very special'

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

India face South Africa test before Champions Trophy

Indian batter Jemimah Rodrigues believes the inaugural ICC Women's Champions Trophy will be a special occasion for the team, with India's recent World Cup triumph in 2025 only making the squad more determined to replicate its success on the global stage. Rodrigues, who is currently recovering from a hamstring injury suffered during her stint with Southern Brave in The Hundred 2026, spoke about India's ambitions during an interaction on JioHotstar's Follow the Blues.India's historic World Cup triumph has given the team a taste of success, and Rodrigues believes that experience has only strengthened their desire to remain at the top."We've tasted success once, and we know what it feels like to be at the top. The more you taste it, the more you want to be there," Rodrigues said JioStar.The inaugural ICC Women's Champions Trophy is scheduled to be held in Sri Lanka from February 14 to 28, 2027. It will mark the first edition of the Champions Trophy in women's international cricket. Rodrigues is particularly excited about being part of the tournament's inaugural edition and believes India's recent success will provide additional motivation."Our team is working towards that, and yes, the Champions Trophy is going to be very special. It's happening for the first time ever in women's cricket, and I'll be a part of it for the first time as well, so it'll be pretty special, and I'm really looking forward to it," she added.The tournament was initially scheduled for a June-July window but was subsequently moved to early 2027 following an ICC board decision. The women's Champions Trophy will feature six teams competing in the T20I format. The tournament will consist of a round-robin league stage, with the top two teams progressing to the final. A total of 16 matches will be played across the competition.Before turning their attention fully towards the Champions Trophy, India will face South Africa in a challenging multi-format tour beginning on December 9, 2026. The series will see the two recent World Cup finalists renew their rivalry across formats, with India scheduled to play a one-off Test, three ODIs and three T20Is.
Article Summary: Jemimah Rodrigues says Champions Trophy will be a special occasion for India. India's recent World Cup triumph has only strengthened their desire to remain at the top. The inaugural ICC Women's Champions Trophy is scheduled to be held in Sri Lanka from February 14 to 28, 2027.

Article Title: IND vs SL 1st Test: Suthar, Jadeja spin India into commanding 178-run lead over Sri Lanka in Galle
Article Text:
India's Manav Suthar, centre, celebrates with Kuldeep Yadav, right, and Rishabh Pant after taking the wicket of Sri Lanka's Lahiru Kumara. (PTI Photo)

Dinusha, Dickwella delay Sri Lanka collapse

Suthar leads spin assault

India’s spinners tightened their grip on the first Test against Sri Lanka as Manav Suthar and Ravindra Jadeja combined for seven wickets to bowl the hosts out for 284 on a rain-hit third day in Galle on Monday. Sri Lanka’s resistance, led by a maiden international hundred from Sonal Dinusha and a composed 80 from Niroshan Dickwella, prevented India from forcing an even bigger advantage, but the visitors still secured a substantial 178-run first-innings lead.India had appeared on course for a much shorter innings when Sri Lanka slipped to 99/5 by lunch. Suthar spearheaded the early assault with flight, dip and turn, while the Indian attack maintained relentless pressure on a pitch that continued to offer enough assistance to the spinners.But Dinusha and Dickwella changed the complexion of the innings with a superb sixth-wicket partnership. The pair added 146 runs from 216 balls, frustrating India through a combination of patience, disciplined shot selection and effective use of the sweep.Unlike several of Sri Lanka’s top-order batters, Dinusha and Dickwella refused to attack deliveries away from their bodies and were willing to wait for scoring opportunities.Both used the sweep effectively against the Indian spinners, repeatedly finding runs from around the stumps.Dickwella brought up his half-century from 67 balls, while Dinusha took 92 deliveries to reach the milestone. Their partnership extended into the second session, with Sri Lanka adding 116 runs without losing a wicket.India eventually broke through early in the final session. Dickwella, who had been dropped on 20 by KL Rahul at slip off Suthar, edged Prasidh Krishna through to wicketkeeper Rishabh Pant after reaching 80 off 115 balls.Dinusha continued to frustrate the visitors, completing his maiden international century from 167 balls. His resistance, however, lasted only one more delivery. Jadeja trapped him leg before wicket, ending a remarkable 100-run innings off 168 balls.The partnership had showcased a vastly different approach from Sri Lanka’s top order, whose aggressive strokeplay often saw them driving away from their bodies and finding Indian fielders.India’s bowlers had made the breakthrough almost immediately after their first innings ended at 462. Sri Lanka needed a strong opening partnership but instead lost Nishan Fernando to Siraj with only the second ball of the innings.Suthar then made an immediate impact with his first delivery, finding a faint edge from Dinesh Chandimal that nestled safely in Pant’s gloves. The young left-arm spinner continued to trouble the batters with impressive control, consistently bowling above 85 kmph while extracting turn and dip.Lahiru Udara and Kamindu Mendis briefly threatened to stabilise the innings, with both finding boundaries and Mendis pulling Prasidh for a six. But Suthar eventually removed Udara, who mistimed a swish to gully.Mendis then fell to Kuldeep Yadav after an uppish push was brilliantly held by a diving Shubman Gill. Jadeja joined the wicket-takers by dismissing Sri Lanka captain Dhananjaya de Silva for 21, feathering an edge through to Rahul at slip.Suthar finished with 4/76, while Jadeja claimed 3/57, underlining India’s dominance with spin. Sri Lanka’s late resistance ensured the lead did not become overwhelming, but India remain firmly in command after a third day repeatedly interrupted by rain.
Article Summary: Sri Lanka were bowled out for 284 on a rain-hit third day in Galle. Manav Suthar and Ravindra Jadeja combined for seven wickets. Sri Lanka's resistance was led by a maiden international hundred from Sonal Dinusha and a composed 80 from Niroshan Dickwella. India secured a substantial 178-run first-innings lead.

Article Title: ‘Easy option is to call for change’: Coach McDonald resists Australia shake-up after Bangladesh shock
Article Text:
Australia head coach Andrew McDonald (Reuters Photo)

‘The easy option is to call for change’

McDonald defends Lyon after tough outing

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Labuschagne under pressure

Australia head coach Andrew McDonald has urged caution against making sweeping changes to the Test side after the historic defeat to Bangladesh in Darwin, insisting that the painful loss should not prompt an emotional overhaul of a team that still has plenty of cricket left in it.Australia suffered their first-ever home Test defeat to Bangladesh on Sunday, a result that immediately intensified scrutiny on several experienced players. Calls for changes have grown louder, with Jake Weatherald and Marnus Labuschagne among those facing questions over their places in the batting order.Former Australia captain Ricky Ponting has also called for “regeneration” in the side, but McDonald believes the selection decisions must be made with a longer-term view rather than as an immediate reaction to one defeat.“There is always going to be a call for change at the back of a loss. There is always going to be an emotion around that from the outside, and even internally. Our guys are sitting in the dressing room, and they are feeling it,” McDonald said, as quoted by the ICC.“You feel a Test loss. It means a lot to them to play for Australia, so let us not lose that in all this as well.”McDonald acknowledged that Australia's ageing squad will inevitably remain a talking point, particularly after a damaging result, but stressed that the current group still has plenty to offer.“It is always going to be a conversation, the age profile of the team. A loss does not help that. But these players have got a fair bit of cricket left in them,” he said.“The easy option is to call for change. A lot of people call for change when we are not winning. They are entitled to do that as well on the back of a performance like that. So that is part of our lot.”McDonald added that the selection process would not be driven by emotion ahead of the second Test in Mackay, which begins on August 22.“We’re not emotional around change in terms of, ‘if we lose a game, then we need change’. It’s the ability to think through, ‘Okay, what does it look like? How do we maximise our playing group, and how do we get the best out of them?’” he said.The coach also backed veteran spinner Nathan Lyon after the off-spinner endured an unusually difficult outing in Darwin.Lyon, who has taken 568 Test wickets at an average of 30.32, finished with figures of 1/125 as Bangladesh's batters largely neutralised his threat. By contrast, Bangladesh spinner Mehidy Hasan Miraz claimed a match-winning five-wicket haul.McDonald felt Bangladesh's approach, rather than a failure from Lyon, deserved significant credit.“I think they played him exceptionally well. As a whole, their batting unit, even against our quicks, they played the ball late, they were very patient and disciplined,” he said.“There was not a lot in the surface at that point of time for Nathan. So it is very hard to judge one-off sample sizes to the function of that attack.”Labuschagne remains another major talking point after scoring 31 in the second innings. McDonald admitted that the batter needs runs but was encouraged by some of the changes to his technique.“We want runs as the bottom line,” he said. “He’s lacked runs. He feels that. We feel that. We’re working incredibly hard as a coaching group.”
Article Summary: Australia suffered their first-ever home Test defeat to Bangladesh on Sunday. Calls for changes have grown louder, with Jake Weatherald and Marnus Labuschagne among those facing questions over their places in the batting order. Former Australia captain Ricky Ponting has also called for ‘regeneration’ in the side. McDonald believes the selection decisions must be made with a longer-term view.

Article Title: 'Didn't help me as person': Facing IPL ban, Harry Brook reflects on criticism during SRH stint

England white-ball captain Harry Brook has spoken about the criticism he received during his only Indian Premier League (IPL) season with Sunrisers Hyderabad in 2023, saying he was caught up in scrutiny on social media.Brook scored 190 runs in the 2023 season despite making a century against Kolkata Knight Riders. His form dropped after that innings, and he came under pressure over his performances.Looking back at that period, Brook said the attention around his IPL campaign affected him both on and off the field."I got into a little bit of a rabbit hole with scrutiny and social media when I was at the IPL," Brook told BBC Sport. I know it's not a nice thing to see people slagging you off, but it means people care and people think I can put in a better performance than I have done that day," he said.Before his century against KKR, Brook had been criticised for his performances and said he was pleased to "shut up" supporters who were "slagging me off".Brook has not returned to the IPL since that 2023 season. Article Title: Sourav Ganguly: 'Dada, this is not done': When Ganguly nearly gave up India captaincy over a prank by Sachin, Yuvraj
Article Text:
Sourav Ganguly, Yuvraj Singh

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Poll Vote & Share your view Was Sourav Ganguly right to feel worried about the prank? Yes, it was too far No, it was all in good fun 3k+ users shared opinion today 5k+ users already voted today 3k+ users shared opinion today Share Opinion

The prank was supposed to bring a few laughs to India’s dressing room ahead of a series against Pakistan. Instead, it left captain Sourav Ganguly so worried that he was ready to give up the captaincy.It happened on April Fool’s Day in 2005, a day before India began a one-day series against Pakistan in Kochi. With the pressure of playing their familiar rivals already building, Yuvraj Singh and Harbhajan Singh decided to play a prank on Ganguly.The two came into the dressing room with fake newspaper clippings carrying made-up statements in which Ganguly had supposedly criticised his teammates for being party animals, irresponsible and distant.The clippings looked convincing enough to leave Ganguly confused."Puri team baithi hui thi (the entire team was sitting) when we created this drama and decided that we will make an April Fool of Dada. Yuvi started it: 'Dada, what is this statement that you have given to the press?' He told him that you have called Yuvi party animal, Harbhajan ko kisi ki padi nahi hai, Ashish Nehra is also in his own world and Zaheer Khan also parties a lot," Harbhajan recalled in an interview with news agency PTI."Dada said 'when did I say this?' Then we showed those clippings to him and said, 'What is this?'," said the 46-year-old.The prank then got help from two senior members of the team, Sachin Tendulkar and Rahul Dravid . They had been brought into the plan beforehand and played along, making Ganguly believe the reports were genuine."...we had already spoken to the seniors about this. I told Paaji (Tendulkar), 'Paaji, you tell him'. And he said, 'Dada, if you have done this, this is wrong'. Rahul Dravid was also playing along, so he also said, 'Dada, this is not done, yaar'. When two senior players said that, Dada thought (this must be genuine)."He said 'I swear, I didn't do this. I'll give up the captaincy if (it's proved that) I did this'."The pranksters then took things further. Harbhajan and two or three other players picked up their bags and started walking out of the dressing room."While he was reading them (the newspaper clips), two or three of us picked up our bags and started walking out. Dada came running after us, saying, 'Arre yaar, wait, guys! The match is tomorrow. What are you people doing?"The prank finally ended when one of the players broke character and laughed."Dada was the kind of captain whom we could fool that day, but later we felt, 'Yaar, we've really put this decent man through it.' If it had been some other captain, he would genuinely have made us pick up our bags and told us, 'Get out of here and go home'."But he was like a big brother," Harbhajan said with a warm smile as he recalled the captain under whom he played some of his memorable cricket.
Article Summary: The prank was supposed to bring a few laughs to India’s dressing room ahead of a series against Pakistan. Instead, it left captain Sourav Ganguly so worried that he was ready to give up the captaincy. Sachin Tendulkar and Rahul Dravid were brought into the plan beforehand and played along.

Article Title: Pat Cummins joins Greg Chappell in unwanted Australia captaincy record after Bangladesh shock
Article Text:
Pat Cummins

Pat Cummins’ captaincy record took an unwanted turn after Australia suffered a nine-wicket defeat to Bangladesh in the first Test at the Marrara Cricket Ground in Darwin on Sunday.The match ended inside four days, with Australia conceding a 228-run first-innings lead before setting Bangladesh only 57 runs to win in the fourth innings. The visitors reached the target in 14.2 overs, losing just one wicket.The defeat was Australia’s first-ever home Test loss against Bangladesh and also added Cummins to an unwanted list.Cummins, who has been Australia’s Test captain since the 2021-22 Ashes, became only the second Australian captain after Greg Chappell to lose home Tests against two different Asian teams.Chappell lost two home Tests against Pakistan — in Sydney in January 1977 and Melbourne in December 1981 — and another against India in Melbourne in February 1981.Cummins has now lost one home Test against India, in Perth in November 2024, and one against Bangladesh in Darwin in August 2026.Bangladesh needed only three Tests to record their first Test win in Australia. They are now the fastest Asian team and the second-fastest team overall to win a Test on Australian soil.Fast bowler Hasan Mahmud played a key role in the victory, taking nine wickets across the match to claim the Player of the Match award. He picked up six wickets in Australia’s first innings and three in the second.Mehidy Hasan Miraz also contributed with both bat and ball. He scored a half-century in the first innings before taking five wickets in the second.Bangladesh captain Najmul Hossain Shanto scored 84 in the first innings, while opener Tanzid Hasan Tamim made 101 off 197 balls.For Australia, Josh Hazlewood took six wickets in the first innings, while Cameron Green scored 104 in the second innings. However, the rest of the Australian side could not make enough of an impact as Bangladesh completed their first Test victory in Australia.

Article Title: 'I won’t accept him': Srikkanth rejects Eoin Morgan for CSK head coach role, says 'stick to commentary'

Eoin Morgan

Srikkanth rules out Morgan and McCullum

‘Michael Hussey should be the automatic choice’

CSK’s post-Fleming transition

Chennai Super Kings are preparing for a significant transition after the end of Stephen Fleming’s 18-year association with the franchise, and former India opener K Srikkanth believes Michael Hussey could be the ideal man to take the team forward. Fleming’s departure has left CSK searching for a new head coach for the first time in nearly two decades. The former New Zealand captain joined the franchise as a player in the inaugural IPL season in 2008 before taking over as head coach in 2009.Over the next 17 years, Fleming became one of the central figures behind CSK’s identity, guiding the franchise to five IPL titles and two Champions League T20 trophies. His exit comes after CSK missed the playoffs for three consecutive seasons.Fleming has since taken up a new challenge, being appointed England’s Test head coach, replacing Brendon McCullum.As speculation grows over Fleming’s successor, former India and CSK player Ravichandran Ashwin recently suggested that former England white-ball captain Eoin Morgan could be among the names in contention. Srikkanth, however, has firmly rejected that possibility."I won't go for Eoin Morgan for sure. He was a good player and a good captain for England.But as a coach, I won't accept him as an option. Even for KKR as their captain, he didn't do anything great. It'll be best if he just sticks to commentary," said Srikkanth, speaking on his YouTube channel.He also advised CSK against considering Brendon McCullum, who previously coached Kolkata Knight Riders and guided them to the IPL final in 2021.“It'll be good for CSK if they don't appoint Brendon McCullum as the head coach. They should say no to both Morgan and McCullum,” he added.Instead, Srikkanth believes CSK already have a familiar figure within their ecosystem who could seamlessly step into the role. His choice is former CSK opener Michael Hussey, who has previously worked with the franchise as a batting coach.“CSK don't need anyone from outside when they have Mr Cricket with him. Michael Hussey should be the automatic head coach. He will be the best choice,” Srikkanth said.The coaching vacancy is only one part of a much bigger transition facing CSK. The franchise's most successful era was built around the close partnership between Fleming and MS Dhoni, with the duo forming the tactical and cultural backbone of the team for years.Dhoni's future is another major question for the franchise, particularly as CSK look to build around captain Ruturaj Gaikwad and a younger core. Srikkanth himself believes that issue needs to be settled before the franchise can properly determine its next coaching structure.“But what will MS Dhoni's place in CSK be going forward? That arrangement has to be fixed first, and only then will everything else fall in place,” he said.That could prove to be the most important decision of CSK's transition.
Article Summary: K Srikkanth rules out Eoin Morgan and Brendon McCullum as head coach of Chennai Super Kings. Former India opener believes Michael Hussey could be the right man to take the team forward. CSK are searching for a new head coach after the departure of Stephen Fleming. Ravichandran Ashwin has suggested that Morgan could be in contention.

NEW DELHI: Tripura chief minister Manik Saha has fulfilled a promise made to Commonwealth Games gold medallist Asmita Dey, with the state government allotting her a piece of land in Agartala to build a house.The 23-year-old judoka was honoured in Tripura on Wednesday after becoming the first Indian judoka to win a Commonwealth Games gold medal.Dey won the women’s -48kg title in Glasgow after defeating Canada’s Heidi Quach in a dramatic golden-score contest. Her father was a cycle mechanic at Sonaichari. Against all odds, she stood firm on her mission and achieved phenomenal success for the country,” he said.The chief minister recalled meeting Dey at Tripura Bhavan in New Delhi after her return from the Games.During that meeting, the judoka had expressed her wish to have a house in Agartala.“During the meeting, Asmita revealed she desperately wanted a house in Agartala. I promised to fulfil her wish, and today a piece of land has been allotted to her,” he said.Saha said Dey’s achievement could motivate more young athletes from Tripura to pursue sport at the highest level. He also urged her to remain disciplined as she prepares for the Asian Games, particularly because of the strict anti-doping requirements.“I urge Asmita to remain alert, particularly about food, because she has to pass through a stringent dope test before joining the prestigious Asian Games. We believe she will shine again in the Asian Games by winning a medal for the country,” he said.Youth Affairs and Sports Minister Tinku Roy, Agartala Mayor Dipak Majumder and Arjuna award-winning gymnast Dipa Karmakar were among those who attended the felicitation ceremony.
Article Summary: Tripura chief minister Manik Saha has fulfilled a promise made to Commonwealth Games gold medallist Asmita Dey. The state government allotting her a piece of land in Agartala to build a house. The 23-year-old judoka was honoured in Tripura on Wednesday after becoming the first Indian judoka to win a Commonwealth games gold medal.

Article Title: Rajasthan stuck in 2012, Manipur in 2023: How actively are states with CWG medals promoting sports?
Article Text:
Are sports bodies of Indian states promoting the game properly?

Medal tally of India's athletes by birth state/UT

Haryana: Hit on the podium, not so much off it

Manipur still talking about 2023

Rajasthan: 14 years and counting

Uttar Pradesh and Delhi carry the same gloomy picture

And then come Tamil Nadu and others

The ones somewhere in the middle

How active are states/UTs with CWG medallists in promoting sport

Does it matter so much?

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Poll Vote & Share your view What do you think is more important for grassroots sports promotion? Social media presence Local sports events Government funding 3k+ users shared opinion today 5k+ users already voted today 3k+ users shared opinion today Share Opinion

NEW DELHI: Somewhere on a muddy school field in Haryana right now, a teenager is perhaps drilling the same throwing technique over and over, just as she had watched on television just days ago. Her sole aim is to pull off the one like Sharmila Dhankar, India's Commonwealth Games shot put gold medallist.Before the 2026 CWG campaign, she, like many of us, had almost certainly never heard the name. And it's not because Dhankar had not won anything before the Glasgow Games; she had, a gold medal in the Women's Shot Put F57 event at the 2026 Fazza International Para Athletics Championship, but because one of the primary institutions whose entire job was to carry that story back from the medal podium to villages and training grounds across the state has, for all practical purposes, gone quiet.That's the part of this story that rarely gets told. India walked away from Glasgow with 39 medals, and for a week, the athletes who won them were everywhere, garlanded at airports, seated beside ministers, their faces on the evening news. But medals don't build the next generation of athletes by themselves. Somebody has to keep telling their stories, long after the felicitation photo is filed away, to the kid training in a dusty school ground who needs proof that this path actually leads somewhere.We wanted to know which state sports departments are still doing their job of promoting the sports and their grassroots on their social media platforms, and which ones seem to have simply logged off. So we scrolled through the timelines ourselves. Here's what we found.No state produced more glory in Glasgow than Haryana. Eleven medallists, including seven gold, two silver, two bronze, spanning boxing, wrestling, athletics, and para sport, headlined by a Neeraj Chopra silver that will be replayed on sports channels for years.Alongside him were names most of India still had little knowledge of. The likes of Preeti Pawar, Jaismine Lamboria, Sakshi Chaudhary, Priya Ghanghas, Sachin Siwach, and Ankush Panghal, all of whom trained in government facilities, under government schemes, and who'd probably appreciate their own state department cheering as loudly for them as it does for its concert lineups.Because that's the thing. The Sports Department, Government of Haryana's X account has posted exactly once in all of 2026, and it's a flyer for the music acts playing at the Chief Minister's Cup.Facebook and Instagram follow a similar rhythm with a short cluster of posts around that February event, and then not much else.Eleven medals, and not one dedicated post to show for it. Somewhere in Rohtak or Bhiwani, a young pugilist training in Priya Ghanghas's discipline would probably just like a little proof that someone up top is paying attention.Manipur's page has an odd time-capsule quality to it. This is the state that gave India Mirabai Chanu, one of the country's most beloved Olympic medalists, and this Commonwealth Games alone produced four medalists from Manipur, Chanu's gold among them, alongside Rishikanta Singh, Bindyarani Devi, and Jadumani Singh.And yet the Department of Youth Affairs & Sports' X account hasn't posted since October 2023, a "Run for Unity" event, frozen well before any of this year's medals happened.Although the Facebook page has had a few sporadic posts here and there this year, its Instagram account has managed just two posts since January. It’s the kind of gap that makes you wonder if someone simply forgot the login details somewhere along the way.If there's one number in this whole exercise worth sitting with, it's this: the official Sports Department, Government of Rajasthan hasn't posted on Facebook since April 14, 2012.Fourteen years, through Arundhati Choudhary's Commonwealth gold and everything else that's happened in Rajasthan sport since.Its X account's last original post predates a retweet from March 2021, and there's no Instagram at all. A parallel handle, the Rajasthan State Sports Council, exists across all three platforms and is barely livelier.Somewhere behind Choudhary's medal is a genuinely good story, but it just hasn't found a home on the one page built to tell it.Gulveer Singh managed both a silver and a bronze for Uttar Pradesh this Games, a rare double that would make a great centrepiece for the state's sporting year. Instead, across two separate official handles on three platforms, Uttar Pradesh Sports has produced little beyond reposts, while its sister account, Sports Directorate, Govt of Uttar Pradesh, hasn't posted at all in 2026.Delhi Government, for its part, doesn't run a dedicated sports account at all on any of the popular social media platforms, so gold medalist Harsh Singh and bronze medalist Tejaswin Shankar, both representing India's capital, don't really have an institutional cheerleader online, their wins quietly absorbed into the general churn of city government updates. Both athletes are, in effect, doing their own promotional legwork.Set against all that quiet, Tamil Nadu feels like a different sport altogether. Its Sports Tamil Nadu handles post multiple times a day, celebrating not just its own three medalists, Praveen Chithravel, Selva Prabhu, Muthupandi Raja, but athletes from other states too, weaving in government scheme updates without it ever reading like bureaucracy.Every medallist got a dedicated post. Somewhere in Tamil Nadu, a kid training in long jump or wrestling doesn't have to wonder whether the sport leads anywhere. The state tells them, publicly, almost daily.Madhya Pradesh, Chhattisgarh, Karnataka's Facebook and Instagram pages, Assam, Bihar, and Tripura all follow a version of that same habit, active, consistent, generous with attention toward athletes nobody outside their district would otherwise know existed.Kerala doesn't run a separate sports handle on X but keeps its Facebook and Instagram genuinely lively, making sure Murali Sreeshankar and Mohammed Basil's silvers got their due.Andhra Pradesh mirrors that same rhythm across all three platforms.Not every state falls neatly into being inactive or staying proactive. Punjab's account managed just two posts on X all year, New Year's and Republic Day, though its Facebook and Instagram carry a bit more life around coaching and departmental meetings, even if athletes rarely get top billing.Uttarakhand was genuinely active last year before cooling off in 2026, leaning more toward government scheme announcements on Facebook, though its Instagram at least carried two posts around the Games.Maharashtra has dedicated posts up for both Sarvesh Kushare and Dilip Gavit, with Instagram staying fairly regular, enough effort to stay out of the quiet column.Karnataka's X account hasn't posted since March 2024, around an unrelated cultural-team event, even though its Facebook and Instagram have stayed warm and active toward its CWG medalists.It is worth asking why this actually matters, beyond good manners. Well, a state sports department's social media feed isn't just a courtesy board for congratulations; it's one of the cheapest, most direct tools available to build the next generation of athletes.A youngster in a small town is far more likely to pick up a javelin because they saw a state government post celebrating someone from their own district. Even when it comes to promoting any government policy, social media can be as effective.Visibility drives aspiration. There's a funding logic too. Sponsors, corporates, and even state finance departments allocate resources partly based on visible public interest, and a well-run social account is often the easiest evidence a sport has that interest.ALSO READ: Anahat Singh: What is in the name? A word from Guru Nanak's prayer, now India's squash sensation Silence, on the other hand, sends the message that grassroots sport isn't a priority worth the effort of a single post, even when the state has just produced a medallist on the world stage.It is worth it because sometimes, the first step towards building a sporting culture is simply showing people that their achievements are being seen.
Article Summary: India won 39 medals at the Commonwealth Games in Glasgow. Haryana produced 11 medallists, including seven gold, two silver, two bronze. But the state sports department has posted just once in all of 2026. What do you think is more important for grassroots sports promotion? Government funding or social media presence? Share your view.

Article Title: ‘That video was not ordinary’: PM Modi praises Lovlina for objecting to distorted India map - Watch
Article Text:
Prime Minister Narendra Modi shares a light moment with boxer Lovlina Borgohain. (PTI Photo)

‘That video was not ordinary’

Mirabai opens up about four difficult years

Narender's joke leaves Modi laughing

NEW DELHI: Boxer Lovlina Borgohain's decision to object to a distorted Indian map during the Commonwealth Games earned special appreciation from Prime Minister Narendra Modi, who described the moment as one that would be remembered for a long time.Lovlina, who won silver in the women's 75kg category in Glasgow, was among India's medal winners who interacted with Modi at his residence on Sunday. The meeting, attended by Sports Minister Mansukh Mandaviya, Minister of State for Sports Raksha Khadse and Indian Olympic Association president PT Usha, saw athletes recount their experiences from the Games in an informal and emotional setting.In a little over 10-minute video of the interaction shared by the Prime Minister's Office on Monday, Modi brought up Lovlina's confrontation with a restaurant in Glasgow after she noticed a distorted Indian map.“Kya hua wo restaurant waale se jhagda kar rahi thi? (What happened, you were fighting with that restaurant guy?)” Modi asked.Lovlina laughed before explaining why she intervened.“We had such a good performance and it was the last day of the Games. It was a happy occasion sir, we were celebrating and I didn't like it when I saw the distorted map. I politely told them and they have made the changes also,” she explained.Modi applauded the boxer for noticing the issue despite being in the middle of celebrations after her medal-winning campaign.“To be able to recognise the significance of that map at a time when you were celebrating and the Games were over, I can tell you truthfully, that video was not ordinary. It will be remembered by people for a very long time,” he told the Tokyo Olympics bronze medallist.India finished fourth in Glasgow with 39 medals, including 13 golds, with boxing contributing seven gold medals.The interaction also provided an emotional window into Mirabai Chanu's journey to her gold medal in the women's 48kg category. The weightlifter produced a Games-record lift of 190kg, but her triumph came after four difficult years following her one-kilogram miss at the Paris Olympics. Modi asked Mirabai about the tears she shed on the podium and even fed her a laddu during their interaction.“Itne aansu tapak rahe the (So many tears were rolling down),” Modi remarked.Mirabai explained that the tears represented years of accumulated emotions.“I was very happy and emotional at that moment. I was crying because I missed a medal in the Paris Olympics by one kilogram. I have faced a lot in these last four years. I was battling injuries and some family problems too.“There were a lot of things. So, these four years were very tough for me. And when I stood on the podium, our flag went up and the anthem played, it was hard to stop myself,” she said.The meeting also had its lighter moments. Boxer Narender Berwal, who won silver in the +90kg category, recalled a funny exchange with a Pakistani boxer after beating him at the 2015 World Military Games.“During the 2015 World Military Games, I had a bout with a Pakistani boxer. I won it but when we were together in the medical room for treatment to our niggles, he said to me 'Bhaijan aapka naam Narender hai, aapke coach ka naam Narender hai, aapke Pradhan Mantri ka naam Narender hai, mujhe Narender naam se nafrat ho gayi hai.' (Brother, you, your coach and your PM are all named Narender. I hate this name now),” he recalled, drawing laughter from Modi.The Prime Minister also underlined the broader significance of the athletes' achievements, saying their medals were helping inspire a new generation.“I have been in this house for 12-13 years now and if there is one group that I have met regularly here, it is the athletes because of your efforts to win medals for India and your tradition of scaling new heights.“Far more than our push to promote sports in schools, it is your medals that inspire people,” Modi said.
Article Summary: Lovlina Borgohain won silver in the women's 75kg category in Glasgow. Prime Minister Narendra Modi described the moment as one that would be remembered for a long time. India finished fourth in Glasgow with 39 medals, including 13 golds, with boxing contributing seven gold medals.

Article Title: ‘From every drop of tears, gold medals are dripping’: PM Modi’s heartfelt message to CWG heroes - Watch
Article Text:
PM Narendra Modi interacted with India's CWG 2026 medal winners at his residence on Sunday. (Pic credit: PM Modi's X post)

Mirabai recalls four years of struggle

‘One family will bring three medals’

India’s Glasgow success

NEW DELHI: “From every drop of tears, gold medals are dripping.”Prime Minister Narendra Modi had an emotional message for Mirabai Chanu as he interacted with India's Commonwealth Games 2026 medal winners at his residence on Sunday, reflecting on the sacrifices behind the country's successful campaign in Glasgow.Modi hosted the medal-winning contingent at 7, Lok Kalyan Marg and heard athletes recount some of the moments that defined their journeys at the Games. India returned from Glasgow with 39 medals, including 13 gold, 17 silver and nine bronze, finishing fourth in the overall standings.During one of the conversations, Modi recalled the emotional scenes surrounding Mirabai's gold-medal triumph.“Tears were falling from you. I feel as if from every drop of tears, gold medals are dripping,” Modi told the Olympic silver medallist.Mirabai, who won gold in Glasgow, opened up about the difficult journey that preceded her Commonwealth Games triumph, including the disappointment of the Paris Olympics.“I was very happy, and emotional too. That day the happiness was greater and I cried because at the Paris Olympics, I lost a medal by 1 kg. In a player’s life what all we have to face. So within these 4 years, how much and what all I had faced, every time injuries were going on and all that was happening.So with great difficulty I had faced these 4 years. So when all that happened, on the podium when I stood, sir, and when our flag goes up and our national anthem plays, sir, we cannot stop, sir, tears come out on their own,” she said.Modi responded by highlighting the wider impact of the athletes' achievements.“This is very good. It is not as if this achievement of yours is considered only your achievement; your victory becomes a very big inspiration for the coming generations.”The informal interaction also saw athletes share lighter and deeply personal moments from their Glasgow campaigns.Modi reminded para shot put gold medallist Sharmila Dhankar of a promise she had made earlier.“You made a promise. Last time, yours, both daughters will become players,” Modi said with a smile.Dhankar replied: “Haanji, right now they are young in age. In the next Commonwealth, one family will bring 3 medals.”Men's 100m T47 gold medallist Dilip Gavit, meanwhile, spoke about dedicating his performance to his guru.“When I was running, when my event was on 29th (July), that day was Guru Purnima, so that day I gave a gift to my guru,” he was heard saying in the video.In another video posted by Modi, gold medallist boxer Sakshi Chaudhary introduced herself and the contingent.“Hello friends! This is Sakshi Chaudhary. Today, our honourable Prime Minister has invited us, the Commonwealth Games medalists, and we feel very proud. We are extremely happy to have met him; he is very humble. Sir, would you like to say something?” she said.Modi replied with a message that summed up his interaction with the athletes: “Jo khelega, woh khilega” (The one who plays, will blossom). “Always cheer for Bharat.”India's fourth-place finish came despite a significantly smaller contingent and a reduced sporting programme compared to Birmingham 2022. India sent 122 athletes to Glasgow, compared to 210 in Birmingham, while 30 of its 61 medals in 2022 came in sports that were not part of the Glasgow programme.Despite those limitations, India retained its fourth-place position and improved its medal conversion rate, with 38 athletes returning home with medals. Long-distance runner Gulveer Singh was the only Indian athlete to win two medals.The Glasgow Games concluded after 11 days, with Scotland handing over the Commonwealth Games flag and ceremonial baton to India ahead of the 2030 edition in Ahmedabad.The symbols were handed to Olympic champion Neeraj Chopra, Indian Olympic Association president PT Usha and Gujarat Deputy Chief Minister Harsh Sanghavi during the closing ceremony.Ahmedabad will become only the second Indian city to host the Commonwealth Games after New Delhi staged the 2010 edition.
Article Summary: PM Narendra Modi hosted medal-winning contingent at 7, Lok Kalyan Marg. Modi heard athletes recount some of the moments that defined their journeys. India returned from Glasgow with 39 medals, including 13 gold, 17 silver and nine bronze.
